data.title: OPEN QUESTION - what happens to sender/group rules pointing at a deleted project?

meta.title: RESOLVED - rules cascade-delete, purely forward-looking
meta.description:
## Resolved

Deletion cascades: any Sender Rule pointing at the project is deleted along with it. This is strictly forward-looking — it only stops FUTURE signals from that sender/group being assigned to this project. It never touches, reassigns, or reinterprets any past 'Signal Assigned To Project' event; those remain true historical facts forever, exactly as event sourcing requires.

On this chapter: ProjectDeletionImpactView previews the rules that will be deleted, each with a plain future-tense statement (e.g. 'Future messages from Mike will not be assigned to this project'). Earlier drafts of this preview showed illustrative past-notification examples with a 'would go to → Unassigned' framing — that implied looking backward and was replaced, since the only honest thing to show is what changes going forward.

On the 'Assign Signal to Project' timeline: ProjectDeleted feeds 'Rules Pending Deletion', which drives 'Delete Rules For Deleted Project' → DeleteSenderRule → Sender Rule Deleted → folds into Sender Rules View (removing the rule). Auto-Assign Signal reads Sender Rules View, so future signals from that sender/group stop matching immediately — past signals are untouched.

Separately fixed: ReassignSignals (triggered when a NEW rule is created, not related to deletion) was incorrectly scoped to ALL of SignalsListView, which could retroactively reassign already-resolved/already-notified signals. Narrowed to only Unmatched Signals (the still-open backlog) — a rule change now only affects signals nobody has acted on yet, never settled history.
